slot.brief: Given rate constant of a zero-order reaction, find concentration remaining after a stated time (or time to reach zero).

stem: For a zero-order reaction $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{products}$, the rate constant is $4.0 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$. If the initial concentration of $\text{A}$ is $0.60\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$, the concentration of $\text{A}$ remaining after $50\ \text{s}$ is

verdicts.working: Zero-order integrated law: [A] = [A]0 − kt = 0.60 − (4.0×10⁻³)(50) = 0.60 − 0.20 = 0.40 mol L⁻¹.

working:
For a zero-order reaction:
$$[\text{A}]_t = [\text{A}]_0 - kt$$
Given:
$$[\text{A}]_0 = 0.60\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$$
$$k = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}$$
$$t = 50\ \text{s}$$

Substitute the given values:
$$[\text{A}]_t = 0.60 - (4.0 \times 10^{-3} \times 50) = 0.60 - 0.20 = 0.40\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$$

Independent check: Zero-order integrated law: [A] = [A]0 − kt = 0.60 − (4.0×10⁻³)(50) = 0.60 − 0.20 = 0.40 mol L⁻¹.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A calculates the amount consumed ($kt = 0.20\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$) instead of the concentration remaining.
Option B assumes $50\ \text{s}$ corresponds to one half-life and halves the initial concentration ($[\text{A}]_0 / 2 = 0.30\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$).
Option D makes a sign error by adding the reacted amount to the initial concentration ($[\text{A}]_0 + kt = 0.80\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$).
